title.narrative: Samaritan's Purse SHF Emergency WASH ES-NFI Flood Response in Red Sea State.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project seeks to provide comprehensive humanitarian water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) assistance to 10,000 people severely affected by flooding in the Arba'at Area of Red Sea State, Sudan. The geographical focus will cover 10 villages of two key localities in Arba'at Alganab, and Olib, ensuring that the most vulnerable populations, including displaced families and those with limited access to clean water and sanitation, receive urgent support.ltbrgtKey activities of the project include the distribution of 2,500 full non-food item (NFI) kits to address immediate household (HH) needs. These kits will include essential supplies such as blankets, jerry cans, and cooking utensils to help affected families rebuild their lives. In addition to NFI distribution, the project will focus on the rehabilitation and construction of seven water yards, a critical step in restoring access to safe drinking water in the affected communities.ltbrgtTo combat the high risk of waterborne diseases, sanitation infrastructure will be a priority, with the construction of 18 communal latrines and sanitation facilities serving approximately 4,500 beneficiaries. This will ensure safe waste disposal and improve hygiene standards, particularly for women and children, who are most affected by poor sanitation. The project will also implement hygiene promotion activities to raise awareness about proper hand washing, waste management, and safe water practices, which are vital for reducing the risk of diseases such as cholera and diarrhea, reaching 10,000 beneficiaries. ltbrgtAs many communities are still without access to functioning water sources, water trucking services will be deployed to provide emergency water supply until more permanent solutions, like the rehabilitation of water yards, are in place.ltbrgtThe anticipated outcomes include:ltbrgtRestored access to clean water for 10,000 individuals, reducing the need for long-distance water collection.ltbrgtImproved sanitation and hygiene practices, lowering the risk of WASH-related diseases and improving overall public health.ltbrgtEnhanced community resilience through the distribution of essential NFIs and hygiene promotion, ensuring that affected populations can recover more quickly from the impact of the floods.ltbrgtThis intervention is part of a coordinated humanitarian response involving local authorities, community leaders, line ministries, local non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and CERF partners. By collaborating with these stakeholders, the project aims to deliver a timely and efficient response while ensuring that the assistance provided is sustainable and addresses both immediate and long-term recovery needs.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
